07 · Headers, source files and module organization

Headers declare contracts; source files implement behavior.

On this page
  • Keep ordinary behavior in .cpp
  • Direct includes and forward declarations
  • Smallest source organization
  • Dependencies and build boundaries
  • Paper2D and PaperZD module dependencies

Keep ordinary behavior in .cpp

Rule: ordinary constructors, destructors, getters, predicates and operations are declared in .h and implemented in .cpp. Why: readable contracts, controlled dependencies and smaller rebuild impact. Applies: even a one-line getter. Exceptions: required template definitions, compile-time constexpr/consteval behavior, Unreal-generated/required patterns, = default / = delete declarations and a technically necessary inline definition. Explain the technical reason in the change; brevity alone is insufficient. A needed template body can use a narrowly scoped included .inl.

// Avoid in ActionStateComponent.h
bool CanPerformAction() const { return CurrentAction == EActionState::Free; }

Prefer a declaration and a source definition:

// ActionStateComponent.h
bool CanPerformAction() const;
// ActionStateComponent.cpp
bool UActionStateComponent::CanPerformAction() const
{
    return CurrentAction == EActionState::Free;
}

In-class scalar initializers are allowed defaults, not ordinary function bodies. Enum/struct definitions and necessary reflection metadata belong in headers. Keep implementation helpers in a .cpp anonymous namespace when they have file-only scope; do not expose them as public methods for convenience.

Direct includes and forward declarations

Each header must compile with its declared dependencies. Include bases and types that require complete definitions, including by-value fields and reflected value types UHT must parse. Forward-declare pointer/reference dependencies when C++ and UHT permit it. Include implementation-only engine/project types in .cpp. Never rely on another header or a unity build supplying an include accidentally.

Use #pragma once. The generated header must be the final include in a reflected header. Put the matching project header first in each .cpp, then direct implementation includes in consistent engine/plugin/project groups. CoreMinimal.h is acceptable for the initial small game module; do not introduce Engine.h, a universal Gameplay.h or a shared include file collecting every domain. See Epic IWYU.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "Components/ActorComponent.h"
#include "HealthComponent.generated.h"

class UStatsComponent;

The owning header declares UPROPERTY TObjectPtr<UStatsComponent>; its .cpp includes Combat/StatsComponent.h before invoking Stats methods. A base class or by-value FDamageSpec field needs its definition instead. Follow the engine’s complete-type requirements for special members and templates rather than forcing a forward declaration that fails to compile.

Smallest source organization

No Source directory, module or target currently exists in the game repository. The following is a proposal for first native work, not an observed layout. Start with one runtime game module named RPG if the created project/module uses that name; use the actual module’s export macro thereafter. Create domain directories only when code exists.

Source/RPG/
  RPG.Build.cs
  Public/                       only cross-module API headers when needed
    Combat/                     e.g. HealthComponent.h, DamageSpec.h
    Player/                     e.g. PlayerCharacter.h
  Private/
    RPG.cpp                     module entry
    Combat/                     behavior and internal headers
    Player/                     body/controller/profile implementation
    Core/                       session coordination and narrow rule calculations
    World/                      area bootstrap and world-state implementation
    Save/                       snapshot schemas/codec when implemented
    Tests/                      relevant native automation tests

Private headers are the default for types used only within this module; reflection and Blueprint availability do not by themselves require Public/. If the project’s generated game module starts flat, retain it until file count makes domain grouping useful. Match header/source domain paths where appropriate; keep nesting shallow. There is no requirement to precreate Inventory, Equipment, Skills, UI or every documented Content folder in Source.

Dependencies and build boundaries

Declare Build.cs dependencies actually used. A dependency needed by exported Public headers belongs in PublicDependencyModuleNames; one used only in implementation/private headers belongs in PrivateDependencyModuleNames. Core, CoreUObject and Engine support the initial runtime code; add Paper2D, EnhancedInput or UMG when their APIs are actually introduced. Ensure the relevant plugins are enabled in the real project.

Do not put UnrealEd/editor-only APIs into a packaged runtime module. Use editor guards or a separate editor module when real tooling requires it. Do not split one module per component or domain speculatively. Verify include/module changes with a build that does not accidentally rely on unity/PCH coverage when available. Do not copy build flags or language standards from older tutorials; inspect UE 5.8.3-generated targets and the installed toolchain.

Paper2D and PaperZD module dependencies

PaperZD is the selected third-party character animation plugin. A project header deriving from APaperZDCharacter includes PaperZDCharacter.h and declares PaperZD as a public module dependency. Direct Paper2D class use also declares Paper2D. The plugin author explicitly requires PaperZD in public dependencies for project use of its classes. This example is a Build.cs fragment, not a verified existing RPG module:

PublicDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new string[]
{
    "Core", "CoreUObject", "Engine", "Paper2D", "PaperZD"
});

Use the actual module name/export macro and installed plugin headers. Native animation instance and notify references include PaperZDAnimInstance.h, Notifies/PaperZDAnimNotify.h or Notifies/PaperZDAnimNotifyState.h as appropriate. Do not add PaperZDEditor/UnrealEd to runtime dependencies. Enable plugins in the real .uproject and verify UHT/linking/affected Blueprint compilation and packaging. Official PaperZD installation/C++ guide (third party). No game build or plugin compatibility test is claimed.
